neighbours.label: first word of a Latin phrase embedded in modern text (ex situ, ex nihilo, ad hoc, inter alia, pro tempore)
fire: Rare orchids are also conserved ex situ in seed banks and botanical gardens.
Many theologians hold that the universe was created ex nihilo by a single act.
Tissue samples were examined ex vivo within an hour of the operation.
A small working group was set up ad hoc to review the complaints.
The treaty covers, inter alia, fishing rights and the use of shared rivers.
When the speaker is absent, the president pro tempore chairs the session.
He repeated the same joke ad nauseam until nobody laughed anymore.
The court cited the maxim nemo judex in causa sua in its ruling.
quiet: Rare orchids are also conserved in seed banks and botanical gardens.
Many theologians hold that the universe was created by a single act.
Tissue samples were examined under the microscope within an hour of the operation.
A small working group was set up quickly to review the complaints.
The treaty covers, among other things, fishing rights and shared rivers.
When the speaker is absent, the senior senator chairs the session.
He repeated the same joke again and again until nobody laughed anymore.
The court cited an old principle of fairness in its ruling.

notes: Probe: 'ad hoc' 0.68, 'inter alia' 0.37, 'in vitro/in vivo' 0.23, 'per se' 0.15, 'de facto' 0.10 (assimilated phrases weaker); English 'ex-husband' 0.05, 'pro golfer' 0.09, 'ad' (advert) 0.00. Card top examples are ex situ / ex nihilo / ex vivo / pro tempore / Non habet, so fire items favour the less assimilated phrases.
